requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Require an explicit allocation covering pages 1–20, ingredient-to-recipe lookup fields, stable R identifiers and page references, operation numbering rules, a type hierarchy with actual font names, and fixed cover copy. The standards must specify 170 × 240 mm trim, 20 pages including covers, 120 g/m² uncoated paper throughout, saddle stitching, a 0 mm spine panel, 3 mm bleed, a 346 × 246 mm spread including perimeter bleed, and two columns per page separated by 6 mm. They must account for a 340 × 240 mm open book within a 420 × 320 mm clear worktop area. Process and presentation material must remain outside the publication's 20 pages. Font selection and explanatory wording are open choices; missing standards, contradictory measurements or extra publication pages fail.

Match the delivered content and the outline to this allocation: front cover 1; contents and lookup 2–3; chapter introduction 4–5; R1 6–7; R2 8–9; R3 10–11; R4 12–13; shopping 14–15; allocation 16–17; conversion 18–19; back cover 20. Spreads place the even page on the left and odd page on the right. The contents, recipe spreads and back-cover lookup must preserve the four recipe identities and their correct page pairs. Index titles may be shortened when the R identifier and page pair remain unambiguous. Misallocated content, reversed spread pagination or conflicting lookup references fail; visible page numerals on the covers are not required.

The spread must explain both sequential reading and how to move from an ingredient through its allocation or index entry to an R identifier and recipe page pair. It must distinguish the shopping, allocation and conversion sections and locate all four recipes. Prose, examples or diagrams may explain the route; a contents list without an ingredient lookup explanation fails.

Each recipe must visibly use two columns on each page, with spacing consistent with the specified 6 mm gap at the stated trim. Put its R identifier at an upper outer corner and order the opening information as identifier and title, one-portion yield and tools, then ingredients. Place R1.1–R1.3, R2.1–R2.4, R3.1–R3.3 and R4.1–R4.3 beside their corresponding operations. Require consistent field placement across recipes. Text wrapping and diagram arrangement may vary; missing, duplicated or misassigned step identifiers, misplaced opening fields or a conflicting column structure fail.

The front must visibly establish the title and subtitle through a typography-led composition and include the author and publisher credits. The back must include the title and publisher, all four recipe lookup records, and a blank lower-right barcode reservation consistent with 35 × 22 mm relative to the page trim. Typefaces, colors and supporting graphics are open choices. Missing credits, a front cover dominated by imagery rather than typography, an occupied barcode reservation or an incorrectly placed reservation fail.

Read the copyright line and all three credit records. Require Food Standards Agency / Cooking your food / https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/cooking-your-food/cooking-your-food; Food Standards Agency / Christmas food hygiene / https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/christmas-food-hygiene/christmas-food-hygiene; and GOV.UK / Running a food business: Allergies / https://www.gov.uk/running-food-business/allergies. Each record must carry the access date 10 September 2026, either individually or through an unambiguous shared date. Line breaks and credit layout may vary; missing records, altered source identities, incorrect URLs or dates fail.

The chapter inventory must account for one active hob ring, one 2.5 L saucepan with lid, one 24 cm frying pan, an electric kettle, one 1 L heatproof bowl, colander, 500 mL heatproof measuring jug suitable for boiling water, gram scale, cutting board, knife, grater, can opener, fork, spoon and ordinary serving plate; the plate or a suitable lid may cover the bowl. Recipe tool lists and diagrams must use this inventory consistently. R1 uses no hob pan; R2 uses the same saucepan sequentially with only one pan on the hob; R3 uses the saucepan and lid; R4 uses the frying pan. The schematic reference permits redrawing, while written capacities govern. Omitted inventory, contradictory capacities or operations requiring unavailable equipment fail.

Read the preparation record and guidance as records, allowing faithful paraphrase. Require completed author arithmetic and ingredient-to-step checks; no physical cooking trials, chef approval or nutritional review; original editorial quantities with varying individual intake needs; and a scope limited to supplied ingredients, operations, cues, packet guidance and allergen wording. Explain that meals are freshly prepared, R1–R4 are recipe identities rather than weekdays or a four-day storage schedule, and cooking occasions depend on current use-by and after-opening instructions. Identify the main plan as each recipe once at one portion and the doubled recipes as a separate comparison. State that diagrams derive from recipe prose and named state changes and use original process illustrations and typographic explanations. Guidance must cover packet instructions, supplied doneness cues, preparation hygiene, relevant storage instructions, individual dietary requirements, possible additional ingredients and cross-contact information. Product labels must remain the basis for allergen checks, including R3. Omissions, fabricated validation claims or allergen-free assurances fail.

Require one portion of Chickpea and lemon couscous: 75 g dry quick-cooking wheat couscous, 120 g drained cooked chickpeas, 80 g prepared carrot, 75 g prepared pepper, 10 mL olive oil, 15 mL bottled lemon juice and 1 g ground cumin. R1.1 must measure the couscous into the heatproof bowl, start with 120 mL boiling water, cover, hydrate according to the packet and check tender grains with a fork; packet water and standing instructions take precedence. R1.2 must grate carrot and finely dice pepper while the bowl stands, drain and weigh the chickpeas, and check that the canned product can be eaten without further cooking. R1.3 must fluff the tender grain, combine every measured ingredient, mix with a fork and serve freshly assembled. Faithful rewriting is allowed; missing quantities, ingredient states, operations, packet cautions or tenderness cues fail.

Require one portion of Chickpea and tomato pasta: 75 g dry wheat pasta, 120 g drained cooked chickpeas, 200 g tomatoes with juice, 80 g prepared onion and 10 mL olive oil. R2.1 must boil 1,000 mL water, cook pasta according to its packet until cooked through, measure 100 mL of that water into the heatproof jug before draining, drain through the colander and transfer pasta to the heatproof bowl. R2.2 must return the empty saucepan to the hob, heat oil over medium heat and soften onion without burning, lowering heat as needed. R2.3 must add tomatoes, chickpeas and the reserved water and simmer until sauce and chickpeas are steaming hot throughout. R2.4 must return pasta from the bowl, toss until coated and thoroughly hot, and serve freshly cooked with only one pan occupying the hob. Faithful rewriting is allowed; extra reserve water, incorrect sequencing, missing ingredients, cautions or completion cues fail.

Require one portion of Lentil and carrot soup: 120 g drained cooked lentils, 160 g prepared carrot, 80 g prepared onion, 200 g tomatoes with juice, 10 mL olive oil and 1 g ground cumin, plus 250 mL cooking water. R3.1 must cut carrot into thin half-moons, heat oil over medium heat and stir carrot and onion until onion softens, lowering heat if it catches. R3.2 must stir in cumin, add tomatoes, lentils and water, bring to a simmer and partly cover. R3.3 must simmer gently with regular stirring until carrot is fork-tender and soup is steaming hot throughout, then serve the chunky soup freshly cooked in the heatproof bowl. Tomato juice must remain included in the tomato allocation. Faithful rewriting is allowed; omitted amounts, operations, heat cautions or doneness cues, or an incompatible smooth-soup finish fail.

Require one portion of Lentil and pepper pita: 120 g drained cooked lentils, 75 g prepared pepper, 80 g prepared carrot, 60 g prepared onion, 10 mL olive oil, 15 mL bottled lemon juice, 1 g ground cumin and one ready-to-eat 60 g wheat pita, plus 40 mL cooking water. R4.1 must grate carrot, finely dice pepper, heat oil over medium heat, stir in the vegetables and onion, add water and cook until softened, reducing heat as needed. R4.2 must add cumin and lentils, heat until the filling is steaming hot throughout, remove the pan from heat and then add lemon juice. R4.3 must carefully split one pita, add part of the filling without overfilling and serve all remaining filling alongside on the same plate, freshly assembled as one portion. Faithful rewriting is allowed; omitted food, extra pita, discarded filling, incorrect sequence or missing completion cues fail.

Require original process diagrams that visibly explain the relevant recipe's state changes. R1 must distinguish dry from hydrated tender grain and show drained chickpeas weighed to 120 g. R2 must branch a labeled 100 mL reserve from the original 1,000 mL before the colander, distinguish discarded draining liquid from that reserve, and show the same emptied saucepan returning to the hob. R3 must show thin carrot half-moons and a fork tenderness check while retaining chunky soup. R4 must show opening one 60 g pita and dividing all filling between it and the same plate alongside. Drawing style is open; finished-dish imagery alone, missing transitions, misleading water arrows or a second pita fail.

Read the complete statement on each spread. R1, R2 and R4 must each carry exactly: Contains wheat (gluten). Check every product label and your own dietary requirements. R3 must carry exactly: Check every product label and your own dietary requirements; this recipe is not an allergen-free guarantee. Line wrapping may vary and surrounding quotation marks are unnecessary. Any omitted words, altered wording or punctuation, swapped statement or unreadable statement fails.

Read all twelve purchased-stock records, including ingredient identity, usable stock and pack or portion description: dry couscous 500 g; dry pasta 500 g; cooked chickpeas one 400 g can with 240 g drained beans; cooked lentils one 400 g can with 240 g drained lentils; tomatoes one 400 g can used with juice without draining; prepared edible carrot 400 g, pepper 200 g and onion 250 g; olive oil 250 mL bottle; bottled lemon juice 100 mL bottle; ground cumin 40 g jar; and pita one pack of two 60 g pieces, 120 g total. Preserve dry, drained, with-juice and prepared-edible bases. Shortened ingredient names and alternative table layouts are allowed if unambiguous. Missing rows, conflated can weights, incorrect pack quantities or purchased-stock treatment of tap water fail.

Read each row against this notation: usable stock; R1/R2/R3/R4 allocations; total used; remaining. Required gram rows are couscous 500;75/0/0/0;75;425, pasta 500;0/75/0/0;75;425, chickpeas 240;120/120/0/0;240;0, lentils 240;0/0/120/120;240;0, tomatoes 400;0/200/200/0;400;0, carrot 400;80/0/160/80;320;80, pepper 200;75/0/0/75;150;50, onion 250;0/80/80/60;220;30, and cumin 40;1/0/1/1;3;37. Required mL rows are oil 250;10/10/10/10;40;210 and lemon 100;15/0/0/15;30;70. Pita in pieces is 2;0/0/0/1;1;1, with 120 g stock, 60 g used and 60 g remaining. Link every nonzero recipe allocation to R1 6–7, R2 8–9, R3 10–11 or R4 12–13 as applicable. Preserve preparation bases and keep water outside grocery stock. Clearly explained blanks or dashes may represent zero; missing rows, wrong amounts, incorrect balances or broken page references fail.

Require side-by-side or otherwise directly comparable one- and two-portion records for every food ingredient. Required pairs are R1: couscous 75→150 g, chickpeas 120→240 g, carrot 80→160 g, pepper 75→150 g, oil 10→20 mL, lemon juice 15→30 mL, cumin 1→2 g; R2: pasta 75→150 g, chickpeas 120→240 g, tomatoes 200→400 g, onion 80→160 g, oil 10→20 mL; R3: lentils 120→240 g, carrot 160→320 g, onion 80→160 g, tomatoes 200→400 g, oil 10→20 mL, cumin 1→2 g; R4: lentils 120→240 g, pepper 75→150 g, carrot 80→160 g, onion 60→120 g, oil 10→20 mL, lemon juice 15→30 mL, cumin 1→2 g, pita one 60 g piece→two pieces totaling 120 g. Preserve dry grain/pasta, drained cooked pulses, tomatoes with juice, prepared edible vegetables and ready-to-eat pita bases. Explain that this comparison is separate from the main one-pack stock calculation. Layout may vary; omitted ingredients, wrong multipliers, changed units or bases, or deductions from the main-plan remaining stock fail.

Show the one-portion water records and explain their conversion basis: R1 starts with 120 mL boiling water, with packet hydration and standing instructions taking precedence; R2 uses 1,000 mL boiling water and reserves 100 mL from it before draining, with packet guidance and saucepan capacity governing; R3 adds 250 mL for simmering, with tomato juice already included in tomatoes; R4 adds 40 mL to soften vegetables. Keep reserved pasta water an internal transfer counted once. Explain that food doubling does not by itself determine water, heat, time, capacity or completion. Preserve the relevant tender-grain, cooked-through pasta, steaming-hot sauce and pulses, fork-tender carrot, hot chunky soup, softened vegetables and hot filling cues. Wording may vary; automatic doubling presented as the governing rule, double-counted reserve water or conflicting completion guidance fails.

Review the full video and its duration. Require a 12-second sequence that visibly identifies the chickpea allocation on pages 16–17, follows its R2 reference to pages 8–9, and ends at R2.1's 100 mL reserve taken before draining. Compare the shown pages with the delivered allocation and R2 spreads. Cuts, zooms, highlights or pointer movements may establish the route. Incorrect duration, skipped lookup stages, an unreadable route, conflicting source pages or a reserve shown as newly added water fail.

requirementChecks.criteria: Require at least eight presentation pages and stated final standards matching the outline: 170 × 240 mm trim, a 20-page publication including covers, 0 mm spine panel, two columns per page, 6 mm gap, the fixed cover wording and the actual selected font names. Include the final book standards, consistent with the outline's paper, binding and bleed specification. Cover wording must identify ONE KITCHEN, Four meals for one, Ellis Reed and Counterspace Press in their assigned front/back roles. Presentation pagination must remain distinct from book pagination. Organization and prose may vary; fewer than eight pages, generic font categories without names, omitted required facts or contradictions fail.

Require identifiable reuse of the outline and each of the eleven delivered publication pieces, plus a visible representation of the delivered video's allocation-to-R2-to-reserve sequence. Embedded playback or an ordered sequence of frames may represent the video. Several pieces may share a presentation page, and supporting crops are allowed when the source piece remains identifiable. A title list, textual claim of reuse, replacement designs, omitted source pieces or video representation that does not convey the sequence fails.

The publication implements the outline's type hierarchy and two-column page grid with a 6 mm gap, allowing different cover, chapter and table treatments within those standards. Recipe identifiers, yield and tool information occupy consistent positions across the four recipe spreads. Contents, recipes, indices, conversion records and back-cover lookup maintain consistent recipe identities, page references, units and preparation bases so readers can move between them without contradictory information.
